# 03. Grammar

Principle: **sentences as short as possible.** Nothing has to be marked; particles are added only when needed. The language is analytic (isolating): words never change form.

Examples show concept names (GLOSSES) and the words in lexicon version 0.1.0.

## Overview / 總覽

| Topic | Decision | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Word order | SVO | I SEE DOG — *ö rö let* |
| Modifiers | After the noun (adjectives, possessors, relative clauses, numerals) | DOG BIG — *let la* |
| Particles | After the word they modify | GO NOT — *eh ë* |
| Adpositions | Postpositions | DIGNITY IN — *önhe po* |
| Obligatory marking | None (number, tense, voice, case all optional) | PERSON = one person or many |
| Yes/no questions | Question particle at the start | Q THOU GO — *ih a eh* |
| Question words | Stay in place | THOU SEE WHO — *a rö an* |
| Copula | Adjectives are predicates directly; BE only before a noun | PERSON FREE — *ken poh*; HE BE TEACHER — *e ët uma* |
| Possession | Juxtaposed, possessor after | DOG I — *let ö* "my dog" |
| Numerals | After the noun, no classifiers | PERSON THREE — *ken höl* |
| Compounds | Existing words, head first | TREE COCONUT — *ihë könah* |

## Particles / 小詞

| Particle | Word | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NOT | *ë* | after the verb: GO NOT |
| PAST | *mö* | after the verb, only when needed: GO PAST |
| PLURAL | *mon* | after the noun, only when needed: PERSON PL |
| QUESTION | *ih* | at the start of a yes/no question |
| SHOULD | *pël* | after the verb: DO SHOULD |

## Pronouns / 代名詞

Singular vs. plural, and inclusive vs. exclusive "we". No gender, no politeness levels, no case: the same word is subject, object and possessor.

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | I — *ö* | WE (EXCLUSIVE) — *ne*; WE (INCLUSIVE) — *pë* |
| 2nd | THOU — *a* | YOU — *së* |
| 3rd | HE OR SHE OR IT — *e* | THEY — *ah* |

## Proper names and loanwords / 專有名詞與外來詞

| Kind | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New concepts, including international ones (computer, internet) | Said with existing words, like Chinese 電話 "electric speech"; once common, a word of their own from the free slots. No borrowing by sound. | INTERNET → NET COMPUTER, "net of computers" |
| Names made of our own words | **Modifier first**, the reverse of the normal order: the order itself marks a fixed name. Capitalized. | SHORT LANGUAGE — *Ihöt Önre*, the name of this language; compare LANGUAGE SHORT — *önre ihöt* "a language that is short" |
| Names from other languages (Maria, Paris) | Adapted to our sounds and placed between two NAME particles, so the listener hears where the name starts and ends. Capitalized. A category word (PERSON, CITY, RIVER …) may follow. | NAME *Nuyok* NAME CITY "New York City" |

Why names need the NAME particles: almost every syllable sequence is already a sequence of our words, so a name like *ma-ri-a* would otherwise be heard as three ordinary words.

Not decided yet: the NAME particle itself (it will be added in the next lexicon version), the rules for adapting foreign sounds, and how foreign names are spelled beyond the capital letter.

## Not decided yet / 尚未決定

- Tense and aspect beyond PAST (future, perfective …).
- Relative clauses: a marker or plain juxtaposition.
- Comparison ("bigger than").
- Numbers above ten.
- Root families (deriving related words from a shared root).
